reconcile.note: Keil and Delitzsch explain that Deuteronomy abbreviates the earlier Levitical law and silently omits, rather than revokes, the permitted locust exception.

discrepancy.note: Colenso argues Deuteronomy's blanket ban on flying creeping things is at variance with Leviticus's explicit locust exception.

quotes.text: is unclean unto you, they shall not be eaten,' is at variance with that in L.xi.21-23, where we read, ' These ye may eat, of every creeping thing that flieth,…and four forms of the locust are mentioned.
quotes.attr: John William Colenso (d. 1883), The Pentateuch and Book of Joshua Critically Examined, Vol. III (1863), ch. VIII, on Deuteronomy 14:19 and Leviticus 11:21-23.

sides.snippet: Even of these you may eat: any kind of locust, any kind of katydid, any kind of cricket, and any kind of grasshopper.
sides.verseText: Even of these you may eat: any kind of locust, any kind of katydid, any kind of cricket, and any kind of grasshopper.

sides.snippet: All winged creeping things are unclean to you: they shall not be eaten.
sides.verseText: All winged creeping things are unclean to you: they shall not be eaten.
